meaning: To be an eligible employee under the FMLA, an employee of a covered employer must meet three cumulative criteria: have been employed by that employer for at least 12 months; have been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the start of the leave (subject to special rules in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees); and be employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) for employees outside the U.S.).

failures.quote:
An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who:

(1) Has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, and
(2) Has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave ( see § 825.801 for special hours of service requirements for airline flight crew employees), and
(3) Is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite. See § 825.105(b) regarding employees who work outside the U.S.

meaning: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted toward the 12-month employment requirement if a written agreement (such as a collective bargaining agreement) exists expressing the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service (for instance, to further education or for childrearing).

failures.quote:
Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where:

(ii) A written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service (e.g., for purposes of the employee furthering his or her education or for childrearing purposes).

meaning: For intermittent, occasional, or casual employment, 52 weeks of qualifying employment is legally deemed to satisfy the 12 months of employment requirement.

An employee returning from USERRA-covered service must be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the military absence, which are added to actual hours worked during the previous 12 months to satisfy the 1,250-hour requirement (subject to § 825.801(c) for airline flight crews).

To calculate the hours of service an employee would have worked during a USERRA-covered absence, the employer may generally use the employee's pre-service work schedule as the basis for the calculation, subject to special rules in § 825.801(c) for airline flight crews.

If an employee is already on non-FMLA leave when reaching the 12-month employment threshold, any subsequent portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after meeting that threshold becomes designated as FMLA leave.
